title: I Enforced the Serger Thread Checkout on the Mentor Who Hijacked My Cones

parts.text: I sat at serger two at 3:09 p.m. and mentor Prue was already running my numbered cones. The card said: ONE SERGER. NINETY MINUTES. THREAD STAYS WITH THE CHECKOUT. I was thirty-three, studio member, holding a stitch card that listed our four. Prue shrugged. "Mentors are the loop." I photographed the card, the checkout, and her seam on my differential. Then I asked for the thread log. At 3:17 the studio pinged why Prue's name was on my cones. I kept my voice studio-soft and let the timestamp talk. A card is only a card until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The studio can see Prue's seam on my differential during our checkout.

social.video_title: She ran my numbered cones on my serger — Part 1/2
social.description: Serger, a mentor on my differential, a ninety-minute card she posted. I logged the seam. Would you have asked for the thread log?

parts.text: Prue called it a sample until the studio asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the card, and the seam still. The cones went back to my rack. Prue ran her own ninety and told the next mentor atmosphere was always about roll. Roll is a word mentors use when a checkout exists. Serger policy now has a second line: MENTORS ARE NOT THE LOOP. I keep our cones on a labeled peg. Prue brown-bags her jokes. The studio finally looks like a checkout, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Mentors are not the loop — Part 2/2
social.description: Thread log, numbered cones, and a second line on the card. Was a sample ever my differential?
